summary: Under lump-sum, cost-plus or time-and-materials contracts the contractor is the consumer of its materials and charges the customer no tax, residential or commercial.

conditions.when: A retail-sale-plus-installation contract, listing and pricing the materials separately before work begins

citations.title: Florida DOR GT-800067 (R. 09/14), Sales and Use Tax on Construction, Improvements, Installations and Repairs
citations.quote: Under lump sum, cost plus, fixed fee, guaranteed price, or time-and-materials real property contracts,

citations.title: Florida DOR GT-800067 (R. 09/14), Sales and Use Tax on Construction, Improvements, Installations and Repairs
citations.quote: Should not charge tax to the customer.

citations.title: Florida DOR GT-800067 (R. 09/14), Sales and Use Tax on Construction, Improvements, Installations and Repairs
citations.quote: include the activities of building, erecting, constructing, altering, improving, repairing, or maintaining real property

notes: GT-800067 is R. 09/14; 2014-09-01 is the earliest date read. Florida draws no line between residential and commercial real property for these contracts; repairs and improvements are both 'improvements to real property'. Commercial (nonresidential) cleaning and pest control are separately taxable services, not construction. Under a retail-sale-plus-installation contract the materials are taxed to the customer; the labour isn't.

summary: A separately stated delivery charge on taxable goods is taxable in Florida when the buyer can't avoid it, and not taxable when the buyer could avoid it (pick up, own carrier, choice of shipping) or the goods are sold F.O.B. origin.

The goods are sold F.O.B. origin (title passes at shipment), or the records don't show where title passes (presumed F.O.B. origin)
The seller requires the delivery and sells F.O.B. destination, so the buyer can't avoid the charge
